destination.name: Oxley Wild Rivers National Park
destination.tagline: Gorge country east of Armidale, with Wollomombi Falls and Apsley Falls along Waterfall Way.
destination.description: Oxley Wild Rivers National Park covers 145,223 hectares, among the largest national parks in New South Wales, and is named for the explorer John Oxley, who passed through in 1818. It is part of the Gondwana Rainforests World Heritage Area, listed for its dry rainforest, and has at least fourteen waterfalls. NPWS says it is best explored as a scenic drive along Waterfall Way.
whyVisit: See Wollomombi Falls above Inaccessible Gulf
Walk the rim at Apsley Falls
Stay in stockman's huts on Green Gully

goodToKnow.title: Green Gully walk
goodToKnow.detail: The multi-day Green Gully walk includes overnight stays in heritage-listed stockman's huts.

goodToKnow.title: Apsley rim walk
goodToKnow.detail: Both Apsley Falls are seen from lookouts on a 1.2 km rim walk.

goodToKnow.title: Check alerts
goodToKnow.detail: NPWS lists closed-area and safety alerts for the park, so check its alerts page before driving in.
